messages.author: 828d260a55f62325
messages.subject: posterior for nonlinear transformation involving two or more parameters
parts:
Dear list

I have the following setting: 
1) a binary variable which represents treatment/no treatment
2) a count outcome (taking values sin the set 0,1,2,....)
3) a glmm with a  random slope structure

and I am exploring the following data/model (see code below) where there is heterogeneity in the treatment effect for each individual 
and I want to obtain posterior information (0.025/0.5/0.975 quantiles)  for the parameter rr (the rate ratio) . 
In the code below I am able to obtain a point estimate for rr but how can I obtain the posterior quantiles associated with it using INLA?
as you can see this parameter is a nonlinear function involving a fixed effect parameter (coefficient of 'treat')  and the variance of (slope) random effect.



Karim


############

nn=1000

ii=1:nn

aa<-5

bb<-1/5


rr<-aa*bb # this is the parameter of interest, the rate ratio (ratio of marginal rates in both treatment groups)


sd1=sqrt(2*log(aa))


z = rnorm(nn, mean=0,sd=sd1)

treat = rep(0,nn)

treat[1:(nn/2)]<-1

bet<-log(bb)

alf<-4

means = exp(alf+ (bet+z)*treat)


yy=rpois(nn,lambda=means)


formula = yy ~treat+f(ii,treat, model="iid")


resu<-inla(formula,data=data.frame(ii,treat,yy),family="poisson")



rr.est<-exp(resu$summary.fix["treat","0.5quant"]+(1/resu$summary.hyp[1,"0.5quant"])/2)


print(rr.est)

#############

parts:
On Wed, 2013-02-27 at 10:26 -0800, Karim Anaya-Izquierdo wrote:
> I need just reasonable precision and Yes, it would be ok to use
> sampling! but how?

Hi

there is an experimental feature called

inla.posterior.sample()

see ?inla.posterior.sample, which can take a result object create by

r = inla(..., control.compute = list(config=TRUE))

and generate samples from the joint posterior, like

x = inla.posterior.sample(100, r)

due to the way the sampler is constructed, you may want to use some more
integration points, like using

r = inla(..., control.inla = list(int.strategy = "grid"),
control.compute = list(config=TRUE))

at least for not to many hyperparameters.

you have to extract the relevant components inside 'x', see str(x) and
str(x[[1]]), and from these samples, you can generate samples of the
variable of interest.


note that the posterior.sample() function is experimental, and future
changes may appear, and you'll get a warning about this when you run
it.

Best
H

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] posterior for nonlinear transformation involving two or more parameters
parts:
Hi

this function is an experimental new feature. to make it quick, we
chosed to sample theta from the integration points of theta, then
conditional on these, sample from the Gaussian approximations with a
mean correction. if all the thetas are the same, then this is either due
to few samples where by random you sample all the thetas from one point,
or there is only one integration point used (like with
int.strategy="eb"). if possible, we would recommend using
control.inla = list(int.strategy = "grid")

to make a better theta-configurations.

if there are still problems, I need to check the code; then I need
copies of the R-code and data...


H

parts:
On Mon, 2013-04-15 at 03:35 -0700, Karim Anaya-Izquierdo wrote:
> Sorry but its me again!
>
>
> In the output of inla.posterior.sample for hyperparameters what the
> difference between using and not using the hyper.user.scale option. I
> seem to get the results I want setting this option to false! Can you
> please clarify?

hyper.user.scale: Logical. Use values of hyperparameters in the user
scale, not in the internal representation


example: hyperparameter is log(precision).

so if this option is TRUE, then this function returns precisions, if
this option is FALSE, then this functions returns log(precisions).

--
